e6db034269a2a10f.body: Small business credit is growing at 26.2% this year and now makes up 23.1% of all business lending. Growth in micro and small business loans jumped by 23.8pp because government systems like UDYAM registration and GST data now let lenders check if tiny businesses are real and can pay back. Banks cannot reach thousands of small borrowers alone, so they lend through partners who find customers and do the checking.
e6db034269a2a10f.implication: Lenders who can work with partners to reach small businesses now have data to judge whether those businesses will repay, opening a large and fast-growing segment that was hard to serve before.
chain: Government systems like UDYAM and GST create digital records that prove small businesses exist and show their sales
These records let lenders check creditworthiness of tiny borrowers who had no formal history before
Banks lend through partners who can find and assess thousands of small customers, driving 26.2% growth in a segment now worth 23.1% of all business lending

8834e38f3d061ba6.body: Banks are growing their gold loan books by 105.5% compared to last year, and this growth has now continued for 12 straight periods. Gold prices jumped sharply between 2023 and 2026, so customers can borrow much more money using the same gold jewelry or coins as security. Banks are winning customers from finance companies because they have local branches where staff can check the gold is real and store it safely, plus they charge lower interest rates.
8834e38f3d061ba6.implication: The 12-period winning streak and 105.5% growth rate show banks are steadily taking market share in gold lending, which is notable because the collateral itself has become more valuable and banks can offer safer storage and lower rates than competitors.
chain: Gold prices rose sharply from 2023 to 2026, making the same jewelry or coins worth more as collateral
Customers can now borrow larger amounts against their gold, and banks offer lower interest rates and safer storage than finance companies
Banks have grown gold lending by 105.5% year-on-year for 12 periods in a row, steadily winning market share

22d3c3a94d23cee3.body: Small business lending is growing at 32.7% per year, and these tiny businesses now make up 23.1% of all MSME lending. Their growth rate jumped by 23.8pp recently, while bigger MSME borrowers are growing much slower—the gap is 11.8pp. Banks can now check if these small businesses can repay loans using government registration systems and GST records, which makes lending safer and faster.
22d3c3a94d23cee3.implication: The smallest businesses are suddenly borrowing much faster than larger ones because lenders can now verify their income and operations through digital records, making a segment that was once hard to assess now easier to lend to at scale.
chain: Government systems like UDYAM registration and GST filings now create digital trails for very small businesses that previously had no formal records
Lenders can use these trails to check creditworthiness quickly, turning businesses that were once invisible into borrowers they can assess
Small business lending accelerates sharply while larger MSME growth stays flat, creating an 11.8pp gap as lenders chase the newly visible segment

164ef9743c99622c.body: The government is paying large manufacturers to build new factories under the PLI scheme, and those manufacturers are ordering more parts from smaller suppliers. Lending to suppliers in basic metals grew 22.6% and 18.4%, chemicals grew 22.6% and 21.8% and 14.2% and 7.4%, and engineering grew 23.9% and 38.3%. These suppliers have signed contracts with big established companies that guarantee they will get paid.
164ef9743c99622c.implication: Suppliers with firm purchase orders from PLI manufacturers carry lower payment risk because the end buyer is a large, creditworthy company building a government-backed factory.
chain: Government pays big manufacturers to build factories under PLI, so those manufacturers place large orders with smaller suppliers for parts and materials
Suppliers sign contracts with these big manufacturers, which means they have guaranteed buyers and predictable cash flow
Lenders see lower risk because the supplier's customer is a large, stable company with government backing, making the loan safer

077d29d64ad90e35.body: Housing loans counted toward priority sector lending jumped 39.0% in one year. The Reserve Bank raised the ceiling in October 2024, so banks moved existing housing loans into the priority bucket without making new loans. Banks that now have more priority sector credits than required can sell the surplus to banks that fall short of their targets.
077d29d64ad90e35.implication: A large one-time reclassification creates more priority sector lending certificates for sale, so banks needing to meet targets can buy credits instead of originating new priority loans.
chain: The regulator raised the housing loan ceiling for priority sector classification, so banks reclassified existing loans into that bucket
This reclassification created a 39.0% jump in reported priority housing loans without any new lending
Banks with surplus priority credits can now sell certificates to other banks, increasing the supply in the certificate market

e0a3bd21e9eb996f.body: Lending to older infrastructure projects is falling sharply: one sector dropped -37.6% and another fell -14.5% this year. Meanwhile, renewable energy lending surged 82.8% in one category and 23.8% in another. Banks that spent years financing highways and power plants are now applying the same long-term project-finance methods to solar, wind, and green hydrogen projects.
e0a3bd21e9eb996f.implication: The same banks and skill sets are simply moving from old infrastructure to new energy projects, so lenders with project-finance experience have a clear opening in a fast-growing segment.
chain: Big infrastructure projects from the past few years are being repaid or need less new money
Government and private money is now going into renewable energy instead, creating new large projects that need financing
Banks already know how to lend against long-term projects with steady cash flows, so they can use that experience on solar and wind farms

b263abfde31bb531.body: Services sector lending is growing at 20.4% per year and now accounts for 28.3% of all bank credit. Banks are lending more through NBFCs that serve services companies — this channel grew 19.7% and is getting stronger. Three services sub-sectors are growing extremely fast: one at 54.9%, another at 41.0%, and a third at 33.7% per year.
b263abfde31bb531.implication: The NBFC channel is recovering after recent rule changes, and a few services sub-sectors are growing three to five times faster than the overall services book — meaning lenders who can reach those pockets through NBFCs are seeing much faster volume growth than the market average.
chain: Services lending is growing at 20.4% and now makes up over a quarter of all bank credit
Banks are routing more of this through NBFCs, which grew 19.7% and is strengthening
A handful of services sub-sectors are growing at 33.7% to 54.9%, pulling the overall services book higher and creating fast-growing pockets for lenders with the right NBFC partners

c102582980584d02.body: India has 12.0 crore credit cards growing at 8.5% a year. Private banks hold 70.9% of all credit cards, while public sector banks hold only 23.8%. Public banks control about 64% of debit cards, which means they already have millions of customers who could be offered credit cards at much lower cost than finding completely new customers.
c102582980584d02.implication: Public banks have a large base of existing debit card customers they can convert to credit cards without the high cost of acquiring entirely new customers, while private banks already dominate the credit card market at 70.9%.
chain: Public banks hold only 23.8% of credit cards but control most debit cards in India
Converting existing debit card customers to credit cards costs much less than finding brand new customers
This gives public banks a cheaper path to grow their small 23.8% share of the credit card market

74189f10e554ddcf.body: India has 13.6 lakh micro ATMs that let villagers withdraw cash without visiting a full bank branch, but the count fell -8.1% recently. These machines cost far less to operate than opening a real branch, yet the network is shrinking even though people in small towns still depend on cash for daily transactions.
74189f10e554ddcf.implication: A lender relying on business correspondents and micro ATMs to reach rural customers now has fewer touch-points, which may slow deposit collection and loan disbursement in villages where branches are scarce.
chain: The number of micro ATMs dropped -8.1%, meaning fewer cash-withdrawal points in rural areas.
Villages still run on cash for most daily spending, so people need these machines to access their money.
Fewer machines mean a lender's agent network has less infrastructure to serve customers, making it harder to collect repayments or disburse small loans quickly in remote spots.

dd55acdd01924a45.body: Credit card spending in the 'other' category jumped 2366.0% in value and 714.0% in volume year-on-year. Millions of people are now tapping cards at metro gates, vending machines, and small shops that just installed tap-to-pay terminals. This is not existing cardholders spending more — it is people using cards in completely new places for the first time.
dd55acdd01924a45.implication: The surge shows cards are becoming a payment method in everyday, small-ticket settings where they were rarely used before, which means lenders may see a wave of new, frequent, low-value transactions from customers who previously only swiped cards for big purchases.
chain: Metro gates and small shops install tap-to-pay terminals that accept cards
People who already own cards start using them for bus rides, snacks, and daily errands instead of cash or wallets
Card transaction volume explodes because each person now swipes many times a day in places that never took cards before

c05213948288e550.body: Credit card spending at shops (POS) is up 9.32 percent and online (e-commerce) is up 4.97 percent, but the actual credit card loans outstanding grew only 1.33 percent. ATM cash withdrawals on cards fell 1.0 percent. People are swiping cards more but not borrowing much more yet.
c05213948288e550.implication: The gap between rising card usage and slow loan growth suggests many cardholders are paying off balances quickly, leaving room for lenders to offer more credit to those who might carry balances.
chain: Card spending at shops and online is climbing while outstanding loans barely budge
Cardholders are using cards more but not letting balances pile up
Lenders have space to extend more credit to customers who may want to borrow

ddc337ecc8ffb9c9.body: Personal loans for credit cards grew 1.33 percent year-on-year, while other personal loans expanded 12.5 percent. Credit card balances outstanding rose 8.47 percent. Consumer durable loans fell 2.64 percent. Most unsecured lending is growing, meaning banks are lending more to people without collateral.
ddc337ecc8ffb9c9.implication: Banks see enough demand and manageable risk to expand unsecured lending across most categories, even though one segment (consumer durables) is shrinking.
chain: Banks are growing personal loans and credit card balances without requiring collateral from borrowers
This happens because they believe people will repay and the demand for such loans is strong
The result is that unsecured retail credit is expanding in most areas, showing banks' confidence in consumer creditworthiness

095119e1af789d0a.body: Card terminals fell 0.48 percent, vehicle loans jumped 17.33 percent, and consumer durable loans dropped 2.64 percent. People are borrowing much more to buy cars and trucks but less to finance fridges and TVs, while card infrastructure shrank slightly.
095119e1af789d0a.implication: Households are choosing transport over home goods, so lenders see strong demand for vehicle finance but weaker appetite for consumer durable loans.
chain: Vehicle loan growth at 17.33 percent shows people prioritising cars and trucks
Consumer durable loans fell 2.64 percent as households skip financing for appliances and electronics
Lenders face uneven demand: vehicle finance is hot while consumer goods lending cools
